candidate.answerReason: The six possible set-size patterns give totals of 84, 100, 90, 96, 90, and 100 plates. The maximum increase over the original 60 is 40.

methods.label: Compare all six ways to enlarge the sets
methods.explanation:
A plate is determined by one letter in each position, so multiplying the three set sizes counts every plate exactly once. Initially there are
\[
5\cdot3\cdot4=60
\]
plates. Only the set sizes affect the count, so we can compare all possible size patterns after adding two letters.

If both letters go into the first, second, or third set, respectively, the totals are
\[
\begin{aligned}
7\cdot3\cdot4&=84,\\
5\cdot5\cdot4&=100,\\
5\cdot3\cdot6&=90.
\end{aligned}
\]
If the letters go into two different sets, the pairs of enlarged sets are first and second, first and third, or second and third. These give
\[
\begin{aligned}
6\cdot4\cdot4&=96,\\
6\cdot3\cdot5&=90,\\
5\cdot4\cdot5&=100.
\end{aligned}
\]
These cases include every possible size pattern once: both additions are in the same set or they are in two different sets. The largest total is \(100\), attained, for example, by putting both new letters in the second set. All \(60\) original plates remain available, so the largest number of additional plates is \(100-60=40\), choice \(\text{D}\).
